q-38245.name: Question 1
q-38245.problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation $T,$ where $T$ is defined as 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}+{v}^{2} \\ {u}^{2}-{v}^{2}\end{aligned}].
$$
q-38245.worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the locations of the critical points of $T,$ we need to solve 

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)={u}^{2}+{v}^{2}$ and $y(u,v)={u}^{2}-{v}^{2}.$ 

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =2u & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =2v \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =2u & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =-2v\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2u & 2v \\ 2u & -2v\end{aligned}| \\  & =2u\cdot (-2v)-2v\cdot 2u \\  & =-4uv-4uv \\  & =-8uv.\end{aligned}
$$

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =0 \\ -8uv & =0 \\ uv & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation $uv=0$ defines the pair of intersecting lines $u=0$ and $v=0$ in the $uv$-plane. Notice that these lines correspond to the coordinate axes in the $uv$-plane.

q-38245.html:
Question 1
?

Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation T, where T is defined as

T:[uv]⟶[u2+v2u2−v2].

a
The critical points lie on the line u=v.
b
The critical points lie on the line u−v=1.
c
The critical points lie on the line u=−v.
d
The critical points lie on the lines u+v=1.
e
The critical points lie on the lines u=0 and v=0.
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Given a transformation

T:[uv]→[x(u,v)y(u,v)],

the Jacobian determinant of T, denoted ∂(x,y)∂(u,v), is given by

∂(x,y)∂(u,v)=|∂x∂u∂x∂v∂y∂u∂y∂v|.

To find the locations of the critical points of T, we need to solve ∂(x,y)∂(u,v)=0.

Here, we have x(u,v)=u2+v2 and y(u,v)=u2−v2.

First, we find the partial derivatives:

∂x∂u=2u∂x∂v=2v∂y∂u=2u∂y∂v=−2v

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

∂(x,y)∂(u,v)=|∂x∂u∂x∂v∂y∂u∂y∂v|=|2u2v2u−2v|=2u⋅(−2v)−2v⋅2u=−4uv−4uv=−8uv.

The function has critical points when ∂(x,y)∂(u,v)=0. So, we obtain

∂(x,y)∂(u,v)=0−8uv=0uv=0.

The equation uv=0 defines the pair of intersecting lines u=0 and v=0 in the uv-plane. Notice that these lines correspond to the coordinate axes in the uv-plane.

q-81279.name: Question 2
q-81279.problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of $T,$ where $T$ is defined as 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}+3{v}^{2} \\ u-2v\end{aligned}].
$$
q-81279.worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the locations of the critical points of $T,$ we need to solve 

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)={u}^{2}+3{v}^{2}$ and $y(u,v)=u-2v.$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =2u & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =6v \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =1 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2u & 6v \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2u\cdot (-2)-6v\cdot 1 \\  & =-4u-6v.\end{aligned}
$$

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.$ So, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =0 \\ -4u-6v & =0 \\ 2u+3v & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation $2u+3v=0$ defines a line in the $uv$-plane.

q-81305.name: Question 3
q-81305.problem:
Consider all non-critical points of the transformation $T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)).$ The inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}(x,y)\to (u(x,y),v(x,y))$ is given by

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2xy \\ \frac{y}{x}\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the Jacobian determinant of $T$ in terms of $u$ and $v.$
q-81305.worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)},$ the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}.
$$

Here, we have $u(x,y)=2xy$ and $v(x,y)=\frac{y}{x}.$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =2y & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =2x \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & =-\frac{y}{{x}^{2}} & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2y & 2x \\ -\frac{y}{{x}^{2}} & \frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}| \\  & =2y\cdot \frac{1}{x}-2x\cdot (-\frac{y}{{x}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{4y}{x} \\  & =4\cdot \frac{y}{x} \\  & =4v.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & ={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4v}\end{aligned}

Question 3

Consider all non-critical points of the transformation T:(u,v)→(x(u,v),y(u,v)). The inverse transformation T−1(x,y)→(u(x,y),v(x,y)) is given by

T−1:[xy]⟶[2xyyx].

Find the Jacobian determinant of T in terms of u and v.

a
−4v
b
−12v
c
4v
d
2u
e
14v
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Given a transformation

T:[uv]→[x(u,v)y(u,v)],

the Jacobian determinant of T, denoted ∂(x,y)∂(u,v), is given by

∂(x,y)∂(u,v)=|∂x∂u∂x∂v∂y∂u∂y∂v|.

In this case, we're only given T−1. So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of T as follows:

  • First, we compute ∂(u,v)∂(x,y), the Jacobian determinant of T−1.

  • Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of T using the relation ∂(x,y)∂(u,v)=(∂(u,v)∂(x,y))−1.

Here, we have u(x,y)=2xy and v(x,y)=yx.

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂u∂x=2y∂u∂y=2x∂v∂x=−yx2∂v∂y=1x

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

∂(u,v)∂(x,y)=|∂u∂x∂u∂y∂v∂x∂v∂y|=|2y2x−yx21x|=2y⋅1x−2x⋅(−yx2)=4yx=4⋅yx=4v.

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

∂(x,y)∂(u,v)=(∂(u,v)∂(x,y))−1=14v

q-81319.name: Question 4
q-81319.problem:
Consider the transformation $T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)).$ The inverse transformation ${T}^{-1}(x,y)\to (u(x,y),v(x,y))$ is given by

$$
{T}^{-1}:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x+3y \\ 2x+y\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the Jacobian determinant of $T.$
q-81319.worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, we're only given ${T}^{-1}.$ So, we compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ as follows:

- First, we compute $\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)},$ the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}.$

- Then, we will compute the Jacobian determinant of $T$ using the relation

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1}.
$$

Here, we have $u(x,y)=2x+3y$ and $v(x,y)=2x+y.$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & =2 & \,\frac{∂u}{∂y} & =3 \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & =2 & \,\frac{∂v}{∂y} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Jacobian determinant of ${T}^{-1}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂u}{∂x} & \frac{∂u}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂v}{∂x} & \frac{∂v}{∂y}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot 1-3\cdot 2 \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the reciprocal:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & ={(\frac{∂(u,v)}{∂(x,y)})}^{-1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-160476.name: Question 5
q-160476.problem:
Find the locations of all of the critical points of the transformation $T,$ where $T$ is defined as

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}(u-1)^{3}-(v-2)^{3} \\ u+v\end{aligned}].
$$
q-160476.worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the locations of the critical points of $T,$ we need to solve 

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.
$$

Here, we have $x(u,v)=(u-1)^{3}-(v-2)^{3}$ and $y(u,v)=u+v.$  

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =3(u-1)^{2} & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =-3(v-2)^{2} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =1 & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3(u-1)^{2} & -3(v-2)^{2} \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(u-1)^{2}\cdot 1-(-3(v-2)^{2})\cdot 1 \\  & =3(u-1)^{2}+3(v-2)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The function has critical points when $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}=0.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =0 \\ 3(u-1)^{2}+3(v-2)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation $3(u-1)^{2}+3(v-2)^{2}=0$ defines the point $(1,2)$ in the $uv$-plane.
